parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Carbon disulfide, $\text{CS}_2$, is flammable and reacts readily with oxygen, as shown in reaction 1.

reaction 1 $$\text{CS}_2\text{(g)} + 3\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{(g)} + 2\text{SO}_2\text{(g)}$$

Table 3.1 shows the standard enthalpy of formation, $\Delta H_{\text{f}}^{\ominus}$, and the standard entropy, $S^{\ominus}$, for some substances.

Table 3.1

|  | $\text{CS}_2\text{(g)}$ | $\text{O}_2\text{(g)}$ | $\text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$ | $\text{SO}_2\text{(g)}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $\Delta H_{\text{f}}^{\ominus} / \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ | 116.7 | 0.0 | -393.5 | -296.8 |
| $S^{\ominus} / \text{J K}^{-1} \text{mol}^{-1}$ | 237.8 | 205.2 | 213.8 | 248.2 |

Calculate the standard Gibbs free energy change, $\Delta G^{\ominus}$, in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, for reaction 1 at $25^{\circ}\text{C}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Carbon disulfide reacts with chlorine to form tetrachloromethane, as shown in reaction 2.

reaction 2 $$\text{CS}_2 + 3\text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{CCl}_4 + \text{S}_2\text{Cl}_2 \quad \Delta H^{\ominus} = -261.6\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$$
$$\Delta S^{\ominus} = -365.5\ \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$$

Calculate the maximum temperature, in K, for reaction 2 to be feasible.
